title: Semantics-to-Contact: A Stagewise Framework for Robust Contact-Rich Manipulation
claim: A two-stage pipeline first localizes the task-relevant region with a vision-language model, then refines fine-grained behavior with residual learning.
layout: 3 columns, left-to-right; augmentation panel, two-stage pipeline, task-progress panel with real photos
description: A wide three-column figure with rounded, colored, titled boxes. The left dashed yellow panel, 'Augmented images', shows a raw image and text prompts passing through a Segmentation Model. It then produces semantic masks and recolored or retextured variants labeled (a) random color, (b) random texture and (c) combination. The center has a blue 'VLM Semantic Localization' box. A frozen Vision-Language Model takes an image and the prompt 'The USB hole on the white charger' and outputs a 2D point. A 3D Calibration box turns that point into a 3D goal on a robot arm. Below it, a green 'RWRL Contact Refinement' box shows a residual module with π_base, π_res, human intervention, action chunks, a concatenation node, execution, real-world environments and offline and online buffers. The right gray 'Task progress' column has robot photos and loss-style curves, with red text marking 80% contact-free and 20% contact-rich progress. The eye goes first to the large blue VLM block.
caption: S2C Framework: S2C decomposes contact-rich manipulation into two stages: semantic localization and contact refinement. The semantic focusing stage uses the VLM to predict a task-relevant pre-contact goal $\hat{g}$ and motion planning to move the robot near the desired contact region. The contact refinement stage then uses human-in-the-loop real-world residual RL to learn local force-aware corrections.
abstract: Contact-rich manipulation requires precise control under complex contact dynamics while remaining robust to diverse visual conditions. However, real-world reinforcement learning often overfits to the visual appearance of training scenes. We propose Semantics-to-Contact (S2C), a stagewise framework for visually robust contact-rich manipulation. The insight is to decompose the problem into two stages: semantic focusing and contact refinement. In the first stage, a vision-language model localizes task-relevant regions across visually diverse scenes, providing coarse spatial guidance and reducing the burden of exploration. In the second stage, a real-world human-in-the-loop residual reinforcement learning policy learns fine-grained contact behaviors within the localized region using force feedback. To further improve visual robustness, we introduce an object-centric visual augmentation strategy that randomizes background appearance while preserving the robot and task-relevant objects. Experiments on six contact-rich real-world manipulation tasks exhibit that S2C consistently improves success rates over strong baselines and maintains reliable performance under significant visual and positional variations. These results demonstrate that stagewise semantic focusing and contact refinement provide a practical path toward visually robust real-world contact-rich manipulation. Our demos can be seen in https://edem-ai.github.io/S2C/.
